ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, what is the internal resistance value of the power supply?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a circuit containing a power source, sliding rheostat Rp, voltmeter V, and ammeter A; the voltmeter measures the terminal voltage U of the power source, and the ammeter measures the circuit current I. On the right side is a U-I graph, with the vertical axis labeled U/V and the horizontal axis labeled I/A. The graph line corresponds to U=3 V when I=0; the dashed line marks that when I=1 A, U=2 V. Reasoning: The terminal voltage of the power source satisfies U = E - Ir. From the graph, it can be known that the electromotive force E is the open-circuit voltage 3 V; when I increases from 0 A to 1 A, U decreases from 3 V to 2 V, and the voltage drop is 1 V. Therefore the internal resistance r = ΔU/ΔI = (3 V - 2 V)/(1 A - 0 A) = 1 Ω.
